## Active Build a 1 Obby codes (2026-09-10)

No active codes have been verified for Build a +1 Obby as of 2026-09-10. The official Roblox game page for Universe 10577682617 and the Creator Group Aeolian Harp announcement channels are the only sources that can establish a code as current, and neither has surfaced a working redemption code on the research date.

| Code | Reward | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No active codes verified as of 2026-09-10 | — | — |

When the creator publishes a code, it typically grants a small in-game reward such as coins or a cosmetic that helps with early progression through the obby stages. Because Build a +1 Obby is a brand-new Roblox Universe (created 2026-07-27), the code rotation cycle is not yet established and could change at any time without notice.

## How to redeem codes in Build a +1 Obby

The redemption flow follows the standard Roblox in-game pattern. If you have a code from the Creator Group Aeolian Harp or another verified announcement channel, the steps are:

1. Launch Build a +1 Obby from the official Roblox game page (Universe 10577682617).
2. Wait for your character to spawn into the current stage lobby.
3. Look for the Codes button on the side of the screen, usually marked with a gift or ticket icon.
4. Type the code exactly as published, including capitalization and any numbers.
5. Press Redeem and wait for the confirmation banner that lists the reward.
6. Restart the stage if the reward does not appear in your inventory, since some rewards only land after a server reload.

Codes are case-sensitive, one-time per account, and can expire without warning. If a code returns an Invalid or Expired message, it has likely been retired by the creator — confirm it against the Creator Group Aeolian Harp announcement before retrying.

## How Fell and Sell pricing responds to supply and demand

The Steam feature list confirms that player-set pricing responds to supply, demand, prestige, and decoration bonuses. That sentence carries the entire pricing system: the price you set is a lever, not a fixed value, and four named inputs push it in different directions at the same time.

Supply is the count of a given item on the shop shelves. When too many copies of the same stock are out, customers stop buying at the higher prices and you either discount or wait. Demand is the count of customers actively wanting that item, which rises with Prestige and falls with stockouts. The two together tell you whether to hold the price or move it.

Practical effect: if you banked three runs of low-rarity crafting scraps and priced them at High, customers will start to ignore the shelf. If you banked a single rare drop with no current supply, even a High price clears quickly. Supply and demand are the same lever viewed from two sides, and the system uses both to nudge the Fair price up or down.

## The Fair, High, and Low price modes in Fell and Sell pricing

The worldeka store strategy piece names three price modes that the game shows on the pricing prompt, and they are the most useful vocabulary for talking about how far above or below the suggested price you choose to set.

Fair is the suggested price the system displays when you click the price slot. It is built from the same supply, demand, Prestige, and decoration inputs above and tends to clear stock at a stable pace. Fair is the right starting point on launch day and after any major furniture or Prestige change, because it absorbs the four inputs without the player having to model them by hand.

High adds margin on top of Fair. Sales slow down, but each sale earns more. High is the right mode for rare drops, items with low current supply, and items tied to high-rarity customer requests whose reward exceeds the markup you are charging.

Low drops the price below Fair to clear stock quickly. Sales speed up, but each sale leaks gold you would otherwise have earned. Low is rarely the right call on launch day, when every coin still has to fund the first furniture purchases, and it is almost never the right call on rare drops where the suggested Fair is already leaving money on the table.

The named modes are guide-source terminology. The Steam feature list confirms only the four-input response model, so treat Fair, High, and Low as a guide convention for describing how far above or below the suggested price the player chooses to set.

### When each mode is the right call

A simple rule of thumb covers most pricing decisions in the first shop cycles:

- Common stock with many copies on the shelves: start at Fair and only move to Low if stock is piling up faster than customers take it.
- Rare drops with little or no current supply: use High and hold it for at least one full shop cycle to see whether demand is real.
- Items tied to a customer request whose reward exceeds the markup: use High and price against the request, not the suggested value.
- Stock you need to clear to make room for a fresh haul: use Low only after the rest of the cycle has been priced, so the leak is bounded and the rest of the margin is protected.

## How Friendly Steps Multiplayer Co-Op Works

The premise on the store page is a group of unsteady walkers tied together for a trip home across a city. Two mechanics drive everything else. First, movement is physics-based and each leg takes its own input, so walking is a deliberate rhythm rather than a held direction. Second, the rope means your balance problem is instantly the group's problem, which is why the store page frames the game around chaos rather than precision platforming.

Gamereactor's preview describes the result as a spiritual successor to Baby Steps combined with Chained Together: awkward physical comedy plus a forced link that punishes everyone at once. That comparison is the outlet's wording rather than a publisher claim, and it is useful mainly for setting expectations about tone.

Voice chat is integrated, which matters more here than in most co-op games because the group has to agree on cadence before stairs, ramps, and narrow crossings. Each player also picks their own look from the confirmed [playable characters](/characters/), including the salaryman, firefighter, punk, cop, and streamer presets.

## Online Co-Op, LAN Co-Op, and Single-Player Compared

Three modes are listed on the Steam store page. The player range covers 1-4 across the co-op modes.

| Mode | Players | What the store page confirms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Online co-op | Up to 4 | Listed as a supported mode, with voice chat integrated |
| LAN co-op | Up to 4 | Listed as a supported mode for players on the same local network |
| Single-player | 1 | Listed alongside the co-op modes, with no separate solo restriction stated |

PixelTwelve's release coverage independently reports the same 1-4 player range with online co-op and LAN co-op, which is useful because it was written from the store listing at the launch window rather than from an older announcement.

### Couch and Split-Screen Status

Split-screen and couch co-op are not announced as of 2026-09-02. The store page lists only the three modes above, with no shared-screen entry and no local controller-pairing detail. If you want four people in one room on launch day, the confirmed path is four machines on the same network using LAN co-op rather than one screen.

## Who Can Actually Join Your Group

Friendly Steps multiplayer is a PC-side arrangement at launch, so the guest list depends on hardware more than on mode selection:

- **Platforms:** Windows, macOS on Apple M1 or Intel, and SteamOS + Linux are the confirmed launch platforms. No native PS5, Xbox, Switch, or mobile version is announced as of 2026-09-02, so friends on those systems cannot join from a console. The [release date and platforms](/release/) page covers that scope.
- **Controllers:** full controller support covers DualShock, DualSense, and Xbox controllers on PC, so a PS5 or Xbox pad works even though a console version does not exist. See [controller support](/controls/) for the input details.
- **Mixed operating systems:** whether a Windows player and a macOS or Linux player can share one session is not announced as of 2026-09-02.

## What Onimusha Way of the Sword Issen Does in Combat

Issen is the named counter technique that sits inside the Oni Gauntlet system. The RPG Site launch-window review, the WorthPlaying launch-window review, and the Steam Community hub for AppID 2638890 all describe Issen as a high-payoff response to specific enemy attacks rather than a generic counter.

The behaviors that define Issen in combat are:

- Issen reads a telegraph. Not every enemy attack opens an Issen window. The reads come from a small set of committed attacks where the enemy telegraphs a heavier hit, and only those attacks are vulnerable to Issen.
- Issen converts a parry into a heavy counter. The Oni Gauntlet parry by itself staggers an enemy; Issen turns that stagger into a heavy follow-up attack that resets the tempo of the fight in Musashi's favor.
- Issen adds risk to the Oni Gauntlet. Because Issen only lands inside the parry window, a mistimed Issen attempt carries the same risk as a failed Oni Gauntlet parry. The WorthPlaying review frames this as the risk side of the Oni Gauntlet's risk-reward framing.

Issen is not a separate attack button; it is the highest-payoff outcome of the Oni Gauntlet system. The combat-mechanics page covers the full Oni Gauntlet context, and the dedicated Issen guide here focuses on timing, chaining, and application.

## Reading the Issen Window

The Issen timing window is opened by an enemy telegraph and closed by Musashi's parry attempt. Launch-window reviews describe a small set of visual cues that signal an Issen-vulnerable attack:

- The enemy's weapon pauses or pulls back before the committed strike.
- The enemy's body shifts its weight in a way that signals a heavy attack rather than a feint.
- A brief visual flash or audio cue marks the start of the committed strike, separating it from the surrounding normal attacks.

Three rules come out of these cues:

- Commit to the parry only when the cue lands. Reading the cue too early forces Musashi into a failed parry, which is exactly what the Oni Gauntlet risk-reward system punishes.
- Treat normal attacks as block-only. The Issen window only opens on committed attacks, so normal attacks should be blocked or dodged rather than parried.
- Watch for the chain cue. After a successful Issen, the enemy stays in a stagger state for a few beats. The chain cue signals that the next committed attack is also Issen-vulnerable, which is how chain Issen builds.

### How the Issen Window Differs From a Normal Parry

The Issen window is narrower than the standard Oni Gauntlet parry window and is gated to committed attacks only. Launch-window reviews describe the standard Oni Gauntlet parry as forgiving across normal and committed attacks, while Issen requires Musashi to read the difference first. WorthPlaying's review frames this as the layer that separates Issen timing from generic parry timing, which is why chain Issen has a higher payoff than a clean parry that is not followed by a counter.

### Why a Failed Issen Costs More Than a Missed Parry

A failed Issen attempt is treated by the Oni Gauntlet as a failed parry, which costs Musashi more than a missed normal parry because the system scales the punish by the parry's commitment level. The RPG Site review describes this as the reason Issen timing rewards clean reads over reaction-time spam.

Reading the window is the single most important Issen skill, and it is what the cross-store demo is designed to teach.

## The three Tears of Metal heroes at a glance

The launch roster of Tears of Metal heroes is three playable characters, confirmed by Paper Cult X, the Gamespress Ruadh reveal, the Steam store page, and the Steam Deck HQ review. Each hero has a distinct weapon kit and a distinct playstyle that maps to a different role inside a co-op party.

- Wallace: broadsword-and-shield bruiser, the easiest entry point for new players.
- Brienne: twin-blade duelist, the highest-mobility launch hero.
- Ruadh Stonecrusher: heavy stone maul tank, the third hero added with the latest character trailer.

Per-hero detail pages for Wallace, Brienne, and Ruadh Stonecrusher are generated from the `heroes` entity family at `/heroes/{slug}`. Each detail page uses the shared summary template and lists the hero's signature weapon, role, and unlock path.

## Wallace: the broadsword bruiser

Wallace is the recommended first hero for most players in Early Access because his broadsword arc is forgiving and his defensive options are the most reliable of the three launch heroes. Steam Deck HQ describes Wallace as the bruiser lane who anchors the front of a co-op party, while Brienne and Ruadh benefit from players who already understand the Emblem and Charm systems.

### Signature weapon and moveset

Wallace fights with a one-handed broadsword and a shield, with a kit that includes wide horizontal slashes, an uppercut launcher, and a parry that staggers most early enemies. The shield bash is the cleanest stagger tool in the game, which makes Wallace the safest hero to learn the game's parry timing on.

### How Wallace fits in co-op

In a four-player session, Wallace is the front-line anchor who holds enemy attention while Brienne or Ruadh players burst down elites and bosses. Solo, Wallace handles the full campaign without forcing the player to lean on Charm stacking the way Brienne does, which makes him the most self-sufficient launch hero.

## Gears of War E Day Release Date: Confirmed Date and Sources

The October 6, 2026 launch date is the headline fact on the Steam store listing for Gears of War E Day (AppID 3010850) and is echoed in Xbox Wire's Gears of War E Day press posts. Xbox Developer Direct 2026 coverage reinforced the same date in first-party video form. As of 2026-09-26, no official delay note has been published, so the date is treated as confirmed for this page. If Xbox Game Studios or The Coalition publish a delay, the release-status page will be the page to recheck first.

A useful distinction for readers searching for "release date 2026" or "release date countdown": the date is a single global launch day, not a staggered rollout. Steam and the Xbox Store are both scheduled to go live on October 6, 2026 in their respective regional windows.

## Launch Timezones and Unlock Behavior

The Steam and Xbox launch patterns differ, and the publicly available evidence does not specify E-Day's exact unlock minute. What can be said:

- **Xbox Series X|S:** launches historically unlock at midnight local time across regions, so a player in New York, London or Tokyo gets the game at 00:00 in that city's time zone. E-Day follows this convention unless an official override note appears.
- **Steam (PC):** Valve's PC game launches typically unlock at approximately 16:00 UTC on the launch day. Region-specific store pages may show a localized equivalent.

The exact unlock timestamps for Gears of War E Day are not announced as of 2026-09-26. Pre-load timing, server pre-load windows and any day-one patch download sizes are also not announced as of 2026-09-26, and the system requirements page will cover PC specs once they're published.

## Pre-Launch Milestones Worth Tracking

Several official milestones usually lead into a Gears of War launch, and the site covers each on its own page:

- **Multiplayer beta** — see the beta page for confirmed windows and access codes.
- **Pre-load** — not announced as of 2026-09-26 for E-Day.
- **Pre-order bonuses** — see the preorder page for retailer offers and bonus items.
- **Demo** — see the demo page for any announced public demo build.

If you are looking for a release-date countdown or want to track when pre-load opens, the Steam store page is the most reliable single source because that page is updated directly by Valve and the publisher.

## AION 2 classes and role archetypes

The Steam store description for AION 2 confirms class-based MMORPG combat as a launch pillar, and the Steam Community hub plus r/aion discussions surface the seven roles that US players will choose from at launch: assassin, gladiator, cleric, templar, chanter, ranger, and sorceress. Role archetypes are reasonable inferences from the original 2009 AION class system (legacy reference): assassin and ranger sit in the melee or ranged DPS column, gladiator and templar cover the tank archetype, cleric and chanter handle healer and support duties, and sorceress fills the ranged magical DPS slot.

The Steam Community hub adds pre-launch class speculation but does not publish per-class skill trees, animations, or stat curves. NCWest has not published a class-design document on the Steam store page as of 2026-09-20. Per-class skill specifics and gender-lock status must wait for dated media, beta footage, or an official NCWest class page before they can be cited as current-game fact.

## How to choose your AION 2 class

The selection framework below uses only the seven role names confirmed by the community plus the role archetypes inferred from the original 2009 AION system. Each class maps to a question US players actually ask when choosing a starting character, and the answers stay neutral until dated media is published.

- Assassin: stealth melee DPS, single-target burst, suited to players who want fast open-world PvP duels.
- Gladiator: front-line melee, high durability, the classic tank pick for group dungeons and Abyss sieges.
- Cleric: healer and support, the backbone of any party composition and a safe pick for new players.
- Templar: defensive support with off-heal capabilities, often slotted into tank or hybrid groups.
- Chanter: support caster with party buffs and sustained damage, popular in organized PvP groups.
- Ranger: ranged physical DPS, kite-friendly open-world pick with strong solo leveling potential.
- Sorceress: ranged magical DPS, high burst damage, glass-cannon archetype that rewards positioning.

For deeper progression paths after you pick a class, see the [leveling guide](/guides/leveling) for quest and dungeon priority, the [PvP basics](/guides/pvp-basics) guide for class viability in Abyss faction fights, and the [Abyss factions](/guides/abyss-factions) guide for the Elyos vs Asmo split that frames most PvP encounters.
